title: Choose an editor through a real consumer
goal: Verify temporary editor selection with sensible-editor, preserving a copy before editing.
challenge: Use a real editor-selecting command with temporary environment settings. Demonstrate VISUAL precedence over EDITOR on this guest, save one deliberate edit and preserve the original. Do not change system alternatives.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-editor.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-editor.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command: here && fresh note.txt original.txt && { printf 'original\n' > note.txt; cp -p note.txt original.txt; command -v sensible-editor vi nano; vi --version | head -n 2; }
steps.explanation: Inspect actual tools rather than assuming full Vim. The guest vi is Vim Tiny.
steps.expected: A private original copy and installed tool paths.

steps.explanation: This guest consumer chooses VISUAL before EDITOR. Inside vi: i, type edited-, Escape, :wq, Enter. These are editor keys, not shell commands. Environment assignments affect only this invocation.
steps.expected: note.txt contains edited-original; nano was not selected.

steps.command: here && { cat note.txt original.txt; cmp -s note.txt original.txt; printf "comparison status=%s\n" "$?"; }
steps.explanation: Verify bytes and the preserved copy. Not every application follows sensible-editor precedence.
steps.expected: Changed note, unchanged original, comparison status 1.

hints: VISUAL takes precedence here; the variables are temporary.
Compare bytes, not just a zero editor exit status.
review: I retained actual output and checked the required contents, metadata or identity, not just command success.
I can explain the stated limitations, demonstrate the incorrect case, preserve originals and clean up only my recorded workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.8 /105.1. Self-reviewed and unscored: the application does not inspect guest results. No full-objective or exam-readiness claim.
